A Divergent Synthesis of Spiroindenes via Ligand-Controlled 
[3+2]/[4+2] Cycloadditions of Zwitterionic π-Propargyl  
Palladium Species with Benzofulvenes 
Yongjie Long, Xianhua Zhong, Min Shi,* and Yin Wei* 
State Key Laboratory of Organometallic Chemistry, Center for Excellence in Molecular Synthesis, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences,  
Shanghai Institute of Organic Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences, 345 Lingling Road, Shanghai 200032, China 
Keywords 
Zwitterions | Palladium catalyzed | Divergent synthesis | Ligand control | Spiro compounds |π-Propargyl palladium species |  
Annulation 
Comprehensive Summary  
 
A divergent synthesis of spiroindenes through a palladium catalyzed cycloaddition between zwitterionic π-propargyl palladium species 
and benzofulvenes in moderate to good yields has been disclosed along with good functional group compatibility and a broad sub-
strate universality. This protocol features a highly regioselective switchable process between [3+2] and [4+2] cycloadditions controlled 
by phosphine ligands with different bite angles. The reaction mechanism has been clarified by mechanistic studies and DFT cal cula-
tions, rendering that the coordination modes of the ligands with the substrates and the bite angle of the ligands play crit ical roles in 
the product regioselectivity.

Background and Originality Content 
Spirocyclic compounds occupy an important position in the 
field of chemical biology and pharmaceutical science.[1] In the vast 
family of spirocylic compounds, spiroindenes, widespread likewise 
spirocyclohexadienones or spiroindolones, are gradually revealing 
their significant potential in natural product chemistry, [2] drug 
synthesis[3] and asymmetric cataly sis[4] (Figure 1). However, com -
paring with their immense potential, the construction of spiroin -
dene skeleton is still running in traditional pathways, which need 
either long-winded procedures or complicated materials, such as 
sequential cyclization of bi sphenols or 1,5 -diphenyl-3-pentanone 
derivatives promoted by Brønsted or Lewis acid, [5] cascade dearo-
matization between alkynes and 1 -aryl-2-naphthols[6] or intramo-
lecular cyclization from complex substrates such as indene -sub-
stituted cyclobutanols and 2-phenethyl cyclic ketones. [7] Hence, 
more advanced synthetic strategies should be unearthed to real -
ize various types of spiroindenes efficiently and concisely.  
 
Figure 1   Natural products, bioactive molecules and ligands  containing 
the spiroindene or spiroindane core. 
As a kind of synthon having semi -aromatic characteristics, 
benzofulvenes have been mainly employed in the synthesis of 
polymeric compounds and transition -metal-complexes.[8] Based 
on the same indene structur e, benzofulvenes could be trans -
formed to spiroindenes in certain ways. In 2016, Jørgensen ’s 
group utilized benzofulvenes initiatively to form enantiomerically 
enriched polysubstituted spiro[5,6]indenes or spiro[5,3]indenes 
induced by chiral diphenylprolin ol silylether [9] or chiral cinchona 
alkaloid catalysts,[10] which marked the milestone of spiroindene 
skeleton being formed tersely from benzofulvenes in one step. 
Nevertheless, although Wang ’s group combined azomethine 
ylides and benzofulvenes together to construct heterospiro[5,5]in-
denes in 2023 (Scheme 1, a), [11] the development of benzoful -
venes to spiroindene ’s synthetic protocol has nearly stagnated. 
Thus far, each method only has the ability to build up one type of 
spiroindenes. Therefore, there is still lack of a diversified synthetic 
method in this field. 
On the other hand, zwitterionic π-propargyl palladium species, 
similar as zwitterionic π-allyl palladium species, have already 
emerged its synthetic capacity in various  cycloadditions.[12] De-
pending on the adjustment of bidentate ligand with different bite 
angles, the electrophilic point of π-propargyl palladium part was  
shifted between 3-terminal carbon and 2-internal carbon (Scheme 
1, b). [12] In continuation of our research interest in zwitterionic 
π-propargyl palladium species related chemistry, we supposed 
that the indene part of benzofulvene was stabilized by the aro -
matic cyclopentadienyl anion after the nucleophilic attack from 
zwitterionic π-propargyl palladium species, providing a driving 
force for the subsequent cyclization. Thus, w e anticipate that a 
divergent synthesis of spiroindenes could be achieved upon using 
bidentate phosphine ligands having different bite angles as the 
key controlling point (Scheme 1, c). 
Scheme 1  a Previous synthesis of spiroindenes via benzofulvenes. b Reac-
tion mode of zwitterionic π-palladium species adjusted by ligands. c Design 
of this work. 
 
Results and Discussion 
We first utilized cyan substituted benzofulvene 1a (1.0 eq) and 
vinylidenecyclopropane-diester (VDCP -diester) 2a (2.0 eq ) as the 
model substrates to perform the initial investigation and subse -
quently optimize the reaction conditions of [3+2] cycloaddition  
(Table 1). As a result, we found that the desired product 3a was 
obtained in 69% NMR yield by using Pd 2dba3 as a palladium cata -
lyst, DPEphos as a ligand, Yb(OTf) 3 as the cocatalyst, Cs 2CO3 as a 
base and upon heating at 55 °C in THF for 4.0 h with 4  Å MS (100 
mg) (Table 1, entry 1).  However, the polarity of 3a is too close to 
the byproduct dibenzylideneacetone derived from Pd2dba3, which 
makes it difficult to separate these two compounds . Hence, the 
source of palladium catalyst was switched to Pd(PPh3)4, affording 
3a in 71% yield (Table 1, entry 2). The influence of solvent was 
investigated, discovering that using toluene, DCE, or DMF as sol -
vent decreased the yield of 3a to 41%, 52% and 48%, respectively, 
and nearly trace in 1,4 -dioxane (Table 1, entries 3—6). The effect 
of different phosphine ligands was examined afterward. When 
other ligands with a large bite angle, such as dtpbf, Xantphos and 
BINAP were used to replace DPEphos, the yield of 3a decreased to 
43%, 30% and nearly zero (Table 1, entries 7, 9, 10).

Significantly, using dppe as a traditional bidentate ligand with 
a small bite angle only afforded trace of 3a also without the for -
mation of [4+2] cycloadduct (Table 1, entry 8). The exploration of 
base effect revealed that both organic bases such as TEA or DBU 
and inorganic bases such as K3PO4 or CsOAc did not give better 
performance than Cs2CO3 in this reaction (Table 1, entries 11—14). 
Next, we further examined the reaction temperature and time, 
identifying that the reaction should be carried out at 55 °C for 8.0 
h, giving 3a in 77% isolated yield. This result was better than those 
at 45 °C for 8.0 h or at 60 °C for 8.0 h, respectively, even if the 
yield of 3a at 60 °C (70%) seems to be higher than that at 60 °C for 
4.0 h (69%) (Table 1, entries 15—19). Finally, we also confirmed 
that decreasing or increasing the a mount of VDCP -diester 2a to 
1.5 or 2.5 equivalents did not improve the yield of 3a under oth-
erwise identical conditions (Table 1, entries 20 & 21). It should be 
noted that the diastereoselectivity of this [3+2] cycloaddition is 
higher than 20  : 1, probabl y due to the steric hindrance derived 
from benzofulvene skeleton.  Furthermore, a series of  common 
Lewis acids including SnCl4, BF 3∙Et2O, In(OTf)3, Zn(OTf)2, Y(OTf)₃, 
Sc(OTf)₃, Yb(OTf)₃ were screened for this reaction;  the Yb(OTf) ₃ 
particularly demonstrated superior catalytic efficacy in mediating 
the [3+2] cycloaddition reaction when compared to other Lewis 
acid additives (see part E at the page S4 of  the Supporting Infor -
mation).

Based on the assumption of ligand -controlled regioselectivity, 
we attempted to find a ligand which can switch the reaction mode 
from [3+2] to [4+2] cycloaddition. Fortunately, ( R)-Ph-PHOX was 
found out to realize the [4+2] cycloaddition mode. It should be 
mentioned here that  although dppe as a traditional bidentate 
ligand having a small bite angle [12a] was a preferred bidentate 
phosphine ligand in the palladium-catalyzed [4+2] cycloaddition of 
2a with methyleneindolinone, it did not perform as a useful ligand 
in this reaction (Table 1, entry 8).  The reaction temperature and 
time were investigated in the first place to optimize the reaction 
conditions of this [4+2] cycloaddition, revealing that the reaction 
outcome was better at 65 °C for 8.0 h rather than those at lower 
or higher temperatures for shorter or longer time , affording 4a in 
78% NMR yield along with 76% isolated yield (Table 2, entries 
1—7). The use of other ligands having a small bite angle such as 
Duanphos or PHOX substituted w ith two methyl groups actually 
affected the regioselectivity of this reaction as well as the ratio of 
[4+2]/[3+2] products, and delivered 4a in lower yields (Table 2, 
entries 8 & 9). In addition, using 1.5 or 2.5 equivalents of 
VDCP-diester 2a did not impr ove the yield of 4a under otherwise 
identical conditions as well (Table 2, entries 10 & 11). Moreover, 
the influence of solvent effect was explored, indicating that re -
placing THF with DCE or 1,4 -dioxane inhibited the reaction, and 
altering to toluene or D MF decreased the yield of 4a to 13% and 
24%, respectively (Table 2, entries 12—15). The diastereomeric 
ratio of [4+2] cycloaddition product 4a was also higher than 20  : 1

The exploration of substrate scopes on spiro[5,5]indenes 3 
and spiro[5,6]indenes 4 was subsequently  carried out based on 
their optimized reaction condition s. The results of [3+2] cycload -
ditions are displayed in Scheme 2; the ORTEP drawing of 3a un-
ambiguously identified by X -ray diff raction is also shown in 
Scheme 2. Introducing both electron -donating groups such as 
methyl, tert-butyl or methoxy and electron -withdrawing groups 
such as halogen atom, trifluoromethyl or nitryl at the 2,4,5,6,7- 
position of indene ring afforded the corres ponding products 3a— 
3j in good to excellent yields ranging from 67% to 99%, suggesting 
that the electronic property of 1 did not have significant impact 
on the reaction outcome. The diastereoselectivity of 3j was 
dropped to 8  : 1 on account of the steric effect from 2-methyl 
group which may neutralize the steric effect from benzofulvene 
skeleton. Replacing the cyan group with carbomethoxy or formyl 
group also furnished the corresponding products 3k and 3l in the 
yields of 82% and 80%, while the substrates having the methyl 
group substitution for cyan group or without substitution did not 
undergo the reaction to afford the desired products 3m and 3n. In 
addition, condensed, polycyclic or even polysubstituted indene 
skeletons were also compatible in this reac tion, producing the 
desired cycloadducts 3o, 3p and 3q in good yields ranging from 74% 
to 80%. Besides, the shift from phenyl group to cinnamyl or het -
eroaryl group, except for pyridyl group, did not restrain the reac -
tion, giving the desired products 3r—3v in 72%—75% yields, while 
the diastereoselectivity of 3r and 3s decreased to 5  : 1 and 10  : 1 
presumably due to the similar reason as that of 3j. The introduc -
tion of para-methoxy, para-carbomethoxy, para-trifluoromethyl, 
para-bromo and meta/ortho-methyl group into the phenyl ring 
generated the corresponding products 3w—3ab in good yields 
ranging from 74% to 77%.  Furthermore, the [3+2] cycloaddition 
proceeded smoothly utilizing benzofulvenes with a carboethoxy 
group or a tert-butyl substituent, affording the desired products 
3ac and 3ad in the yields of 74% and 36% , respectively. Moreover, 
we also examined the reaction outcome with VDCP -diesters 2 
bearing different ester groups. The variation of diester ’s moiety 
slightly influenced the reaction results, delivering the corresponding 
products 3ae—3ag in the yields of 67%—78%, while inserting an 
ethyl group to the terminal position of allene provided the desired 
product 3ah in the yield of 76% with the diastereomeric ratio of 
1.7 : 1, due to the introduction of an allenyl axial chirality. 
The results of the study on the substrate universality of [4+2] 
cycloaddition are generally similar to the [3+2] cycloaddition 
mode, which are exhibited in Scheme 3 along with the ORTEP 
drawing of  4b unequivocally determined by X -ray diffraction. 
When the DPEphos ligand with a large bite angle was replaced by 
the (R)-Ph-PHOX ligand with a small bite angle, the excellent dia -
stereoselectivity was inherited and the regioselectivity on spi -
ro[5,6]indene to spiro[5,5]indene ratio can be kept over 16  : 1 in 
most cases. Analogously, the introduction of electron -donating 
groups as well as electron -withdrawing group at the 4,5,6,7-posi-
tion of indene ring or varying diverse electron -withdrawing group 
at 1-position of indene ring afforded the corresponding products 
4a—4i in moderate to good yields ranging from 4 4% to 76%. In 
the case of naphthobenzofulvene, the ratio of [4+2] cycloadduct 
4h and [3+2] cycloadduct as 3o in Scheme 2 decreased to 10  : 1. 
Heteroaryl groups are compatible with this [4+2] cycloaddition, 
giving the desired products 4j and 4k with 2 -furanyl or 2 -thienyl 
moiety in 64% and 62% yields, although their diastereomeric rati -
os decreased to 10  : 1 and 11  : 1, respectively. In addition, the 
functional group tolerance of the exo cyclic-olefinic moiety in 
benzofulvenes exhibited semblable peculiarity as those of spi -
ro[5,5]indenes described in Scheme 2, affording spiro[5,6]indenes 
4l—4r in 52% to 70% yields. However, an exocyclic carboethoxy 
instead of a phenyl group gave the desired product 4s in 19% yield 
and 5  : 1 regioselectivity. Besides, the reactivity of different 
VDCP-diesters 2 was also tested in this [4+2] cycloaddition, af -
fording the corresponding products 4t—4w in 56% to 68% yields. 
Interestingly, the diastereoselectivity for 4u (> 20 : 1) and 4v (14 : 1) 
seems to be reversed as compared with 3ad (> 20 : 1) and 3ae (10 : 
1) in the [3+2] cycloaddition  shown in Scheme 2, perhaps due to 
the mutual steric effect between ligand and the substrates. VDCP 
diester with an ethyl unit at the terminal position of allene fur-
nished the desired product 4w in 4  : 1 regioselectivity along with 
high diastereoselectivity.

practicability of this method on a large -scale was next assessed.

Moreover, the further conversions of 3a and 4a were also 
conducted as shown in Scheme 4, c. Aminolysis of the carbo -
ethoxy groups upon treating 3a with NaOMe in formamide at 
75 °C produced 3a-I in 67% yield, which was derived from a fur -
ther Michael addition on the vinylcyanide moiety after the ami -
nolysis reaction. Moreover, a difunctionalization process of ter -
minal allene with SIMesCuCl and (BPin) 2 in the presence of KO tBu 
and EtI developed by Ito ’s group[13] was also used in the transfor -
mation of 3a, generating 3a-II in 87% yield in DMF at room tem -
perature; 3a probably went through an insertion of alkenyl-copper 
species to conjugated cyanide due to the inductive effect brought 
from the conjugated cyanide similar as that of aminolysis reaction. 
The structures of 3a-I and 3a-II have been unambiguously identi -
fied by X -ray diffraction and their ORTEP drawings are shown in 
Scheme 4. On the other hand,  4a could be transformed to the 
corresponding epoxide 4a-I in 74% yield along with 1.5  : 1 dia -
stereomeric ratio through an epoxidation upon treating with 
m-CPBA and Na2CO3 in THF. 
In order to clarify the mechanism of this reaction, a series of 
control experiments were performed to probe the reaction path -
ways (Scheme 5). Neither [3+2] nor [4+2] cycloaddition occurred 
in the absence of palladium resources, while removing Yb(OTf) 3 
led to the lower yields for both two types of cycloadditions. Hence, 
palladium as the basic catalyst and Yb(OTf)3 as the cocatalyst were 
confirmed. In addition, using Pd(PPh 3)4 as the palladium source 
gave the [3+2] cycloaddition product 3a in 28% yield in absence of 
DPEphos and none of the [4+2] cycloaddition product 4a was 
formed in the absence of ( R)-Ph-PHOX ligand, rendering that the 
bidentate ligand plays a key role in these cycloaddition reactions. 
On the basis of the above experimental results and our previ -
ous investigations on the reaction pathways,[12,14] a plausible reac-
tion mechanism was proposed in Scheme 6. The zwitterionic 
π-propargyl palladium species I, generated from an oxidative ad -
dition between ligand -coordinated Pd(0) and Yb 3+-coordinated 
VDCP-diester 2a, launches a nucleophilic  attack to the exocyclic 
position of benzofulvene 1a, forming an intermediate II stabilized 
by the aromaticity of cyclopentadienyl anion. When palladium 
catalyst coordinates with DPEphos, a bidentate ligand with a large 
bite angle, the cyclopentadienyl ani on tends to attack onto the 
carbon atom at 3-position of the π-propargyl palladium species to 
provide [3+2] cycloaddition intermediate III-3-pre, and subse -
quently produces spiro[5,5]indene 3a through a ligand exchange 
process with 2a along with the regene ration of the zwitterionic 
π-propargyl palladium species I to complete the catalytic cycle . 
Whereas, the cyclopentadienyl anion is more likely to approach 
onto the carbon atom at 2-position of π-propargyl palladium spe-
cies if palladium catalyst is coordin ated by ( R)-Ph-PHOX, a special 
bidentate ligand with a small bite angle, affording palladacyclo -
butene species III,[15] which can be formed in a similar way as that 
of palladacyclobutane derived from π-allyl palladium species. [15] 
Then, the palladium intermediate III shall undergo a base-induced 
protonation to form a π-allyl palladium species IV, which under -
goes a β-H elimination to furnish the [4+2] cycloaddition interme-
diate V-4-pre. A ligand exchange process between V-4-pre and 2a 
affords spiro[5,6]indene 4a and regenerates t he zwitterionic 
π-propargyl palladium species I to complete the catalytic cycle. 
As shown in Scheme 6, the selectivity originates from the cy -
clopentadienyl anion moiety of the intermediate II attacking dif-
ferent carbon of π-propargyl palladium moiety.  Thus, density 
functional theory (DFT) calculation was used to investigate the 
selectivity-determining step (Figure 2). When DPEphos is utilized 
as the ligand, the cycloaddition can undergo two pathways origi -
nated from η1/η3 type intermediates INT A-1 or INT A-1’ to form 
[3+2] product or [4+2] product. Although the energy of interme -
diate INT A-1’ is lower than that of INT A-1 by 13.7 kcal/mol, the

an energy gap of 15.1 kcal/mol between two transition states and 
an energy gap of 4.1 kcal/mol between the two products. We spec-
ulate that DPEphos with a large bite angle, which is  about 104°— 
108°  upon coordinating with palladium source, would produce 
more steric hindrance, thereby restraining the formation of TS A’ 
from INT A-1’ and raising the energy barrier of [4+2] type reaction; 
(R)-Ph-PHOX with a small bite angle, that is about 81°—90°  upon co-
ordinating with palladium source, results in much smaller energy 
barrier for generation of the [4+2] product due to the steric effect. 
Conclusions
 
In summary, a ligand -controlled divergent [3+2]/[4+2] cy -
cloaddition between benzofulvenes and zwitterionic π-propargyl 
palladium species generated from VDCP -diesters has been estab -
lished for the rapid construction of substituted spiro[5,5]indenes 
and spiro[5,6]indenes in moderate to excellent yields with good 
functional group toleration and a broad substrate scope . The 
plausible mechanistic paradigm was proposed based on the  con-
trol experiments and our previous work, rendering that the reac -
tion proceeds  through a zwitterionic π-propargyl palladium spe -
cies, a key intermediate in these cycloaddition reactions. The 
large-scale synthesis and the further conversion of the obtained 
cyclized products indicated that this synthetic method can easily 
access multi -substituted endocyclic compounds, polycyclic com -
pounds or epoxide substances. The DFT calculations reveal the 
origin of product selectivity. The further applications of this 
methodology in the preparing bioactive substances or drug -like 
molecules are also undergoing in our laboratory.

Comprehensive Summary

A divergent synthesis of spiroindenes through a palladium catalyzed cycloaddition between zwitterionic π-propargyl palladium species
and benzofulvenes in moderate to good yields has been disclosed along with good functional group compatibility and a broad sub-
strate universality. This protocol features a highly regioselective switchable process between [3+2] and [4+2] cycloadditions controlled
by phosphine ligands with different bite angles. The reaction mechanism has been clarified by mechanistic studies and DFT calcula-
tions, rendering that the coordination modes of the ligands with the substrates and the bite angle of the ligands play critical roles in
the product regioselectivity.
Background and Originality Content

Spirocyclic compounds occupy an important position in the
field of chemical biology and pharmaceutical science.<sup>[1]</sup> In the vast
family of spirocylic compounds, spiroindenes, widespread likewise
spirocyclohexadienones or spiroindolones, are gradually revealing
their significant potential in natural product chemistry,<sup>[2]</sup> drug
synthesis<sup>[3]</sup> and asymmetric catalysis<sup>[4]</sup> (Figure 1). However, com-
paring with their immense potential, the construction of spiroin-
dene skeleton is still running in traditional pathways, which need
either long-winded procedures or complicated materials, such as
sequential cyclization of bisphenols or 1,5-diphenyl-3-pentanone
derivatives promoted by Brønsted or Lewis acid,<sup>[5]</sup> cascade dearo-
matization between alkynes and 1-aryl-2-naphthols<sup>[6]</sup> or intramo-
lecular cyclization from complex substrates such as indene-sub-
stituted cyclobutanols and 2-phenethyl cyclic ketones.<sup>[7]</sup> Hence,
more advanced synthetic strategies should be unearthed to real-
ize various types of spiroindenes efficiently and concisely.

Figure 1 Natural products, bioactive molecules and ligands containing
the spiroindene or spiroindane core.

As a kind of synthon having semi-aromatic characteristics,
benzofulvenes have been mainly employed in the synthesis of
polymeric compounds and transition-metal-complexes.<sup>[8]</sup> Based
on the same indene structure, benzofulvenes could be trans-
formed to spiroindenes in certain ways. In 2016, Jørgensen’s
group utilized benzofulvenes initiatively to form enantiomerically
enriched polysubstituted spiro[5,6]indenes or spiro[5,3]indenes
induced by chiral diphenylprolinol silylether<sup>[9]</sup> or chiral cinchona
alkaloid catalysts,<sup>[10]</sup> which marked the milestone of spiroindene
skeleton being formed tersely from benzofulvenes in one step.
Nevertheless, although Wang’s group combined azomethine
ylides and benzofulvenes together to construct heterospiro[5,5]in-
denes in 2023 (Scheme 1, a),<sup>[11]</sup> the development of benzoful-
venes to spiroindene’s synthetic protocol has nearly stagnated.
Thus far, each method only has the ability to build up one type of
spiroindenes. Therefore, there is still lack of a diversified synthetic
method in this field.

On the other hand, zwitterionic π-propargyl palladium species,
similar as zwitterionic π-allyl palladium species, have already
emerged its synthetic capacity in various cycloadditions.<sup>[12]</sup> De-
pending on the adjustment of bidentate ligand with different bite
angles, the electrophilic point of π-propargyl palladium part was
shifted between 3-terminal carbon and 2-internal carbon (Scheme
1, b).<sup>[12]</sup> In continuation of our research interest in zwitterionic
π-propargyl palladium species related chemistry, we supposed
that the indene part of benzofulvene was stabilized by the aro-
matic cyclopentadienyl anion after the nucleophilic attack from
zwitterionic π-propargyl palladium species, providing a driving
force for the subsequent cyclization. Thus, we anticipate that a

divergent synthesis of spiroindenes could be achieved upon using
bidentate phosphine ligands having different bite angles as the
key controlling point (Scheme 1, c).

In order to clarify the mechanism of this reaction, a series of
control experiments were performed to probe the reaction path-
ways (Scheme 5). Neither [3+2] nor [4+2] cycloaddition occurred
in the absence of palladium resources, while removing Yb(OTf)
led to the lower yields for both two types of cycloadditions. Hence,
palladium as the basic catalyst and Yb(OTf) as the cocatalyst were
confirmed. In addition, using Pd(PPh<sub>3</sub>)<sub>4</sub> as the palladium source
gave the [3+2] cycloaddition product 3a in 28% yield in absence of
DPEphos and none of the [4+2] cycloaddition product 4a was
formed in the absence of (R)-Ph-PHOX ligand, rendering that the
bidentate ligand plays a key role in these cycloaddition reactions.

On the basis of the above experimental results and our previ-

tion mechanism was proposed in Scheme 6. The zwitterionic
π-propargyl palladium species I, generated from an oxidative ad-

VDCP-diester 2a, launches a nucleophilic attack to the exocyclic
position of benzofulvene 1a, forming an intermediate II stabilized
by the aromaticity of cyclopentadienyl anion. When palladium
catalyst coordinates with DPEphos, a bidentate ligand with a large
bite angle, the cyclopentadienyl anion tends to attack onto the
carbon atom at 3-position of the π-propargyl palladium species to

process with 2a along with the regeneration of the zwitterionic
π-propargyl palladium species I to complete the catalytic cycle.
Whereas, the cyclopentadienyl anion is more likely to approach
onto the carbon atom at 2-position of π-propargyl palladium spe-

cies if palladium catalyst is coordinated by (R)-Ph-PHOX, a special
bidentate ligand with a small bite angle, affording palladacyclo-
butene species

which can be formed in a similar way as that
of palladacyclobutane derived from π-allyl palladium species.<sup>[15]</sup>
Then, the palladium intermediate III shall undergo a base-induced

Conclusions

In summary, a ligand-controlled divergent
[ 3 + 2 ] / [ 4 + 2 ]
cy-
cloaddition between benzofulvenes and zwitterionic π-propargyl
palladium species generated from VDCP-diesters has been estab-
lished for the rapid construction of substituted spiro[5,5]indenes
and spiro[5,6]indenes in moderate to excellent yields with good
functional group toleration and a broad substrate scope. The
plausible mechanistic paradigm was proposed based on the con-
trol experiments and our previous work, rendering that the reac-
tion proceeds through a zwitterionic π-propargyl palladium spe-
cies, a key intermediate in these cycloaddition reactions. The
large-scale synthesis and the further conversion of the obtained
cyclized products indicated that this synthetic method can easily
access multi-substituted endocyclic compounds, polycyclic com-
pounds or epoxide substances. The DFT calculations reveal the
origin of product selectivity. The further applications of this
methodology in the preparing bioactive substances or drug-like
molecules are also undergoing in our laboratory.
